acceptance_examples: Every baseline CLI command, MCP tool, portable agent, and built JavaScript export remains available.
Existing valid and invalid inputs keep their output shapes, safety decisions, and exit behavior.
The CLI dispatch, MCP error handling, fact checks, and Stage 1 evaluation use named bounded functions instead of long mixed-responsibility flows.
A new user can install the package, run the basic workflow, and find every command from the README.
The README uses simple technical English and links to detailed contracts instead of repeating them.
The source tests, release audit, Claude bundle, npm tarball, clean install smoke test, and pull request CI all pass on the same revision.

tracks.evidence: npm test and focused module tests

tracks.reason: README quality and merge readiness are acceptance and integration concerns, not isolated code units.

tracks.evidence: CLI, MCP, agent, export, and README command inventory comparisons
release audit, Claude bundle, npm pack, clean install smoke test, and GitHub CI
